Jennifer, Kellie, and Kyle,

I’m wrapping up final tasks in my last few days in the office and wanted to circle back on
a few things I had noted as outstanding requests from the GBOS team from our last
quarterly meeting. Apologies for the delay in getting back to you on these items.

First, I had a note that you had asked why municipal assessed value does not appear
to track with the increase and decrease in the market value of a home and, as a
corollary, why so many homes in Girdwood experienced changes in assessed value
this year.

Jack, our Municipal Assessor, helped me with the following response:

     For 2026, Property Appraisal updated parts of the residential assessment model to
      better reflect current market information and align better with national
     assessment standards. The basic approach to valuing homes did not change, but
    some of the information used in the model was updated, including construction
     cost data, home quality categories, and the way homes are grouped into market
      areas. In Girdwood, those updates were combined with a larger local market
     adjustment than most residential areas received. Put simply, recent market data
    showed that Girdwood assessments had not kept pace with the market, so the
     2026 Girdwood values included both the general model updates and an additional
     market correction.

Jack is cc’d here, so that you might follow up with him directly with any follow up
questions.

Additionally, I had a note that you had asked about why a traffic study has not been
completed by the Municipality as part of the Holtan Hills development, and whether
such a study might still be a possibility.

Tiffany from Real Estate and Greg Soule from Development Services helped me with info
informing the following response:

As I know you all know, the Municipal Traffic Department does not directly
     complete traffic studies related to specific private developments (it is not
     adequately resourced to do so). A traffic study requirement is imposed on a
     developer as a condition of approval on the platting action for the new
     development. With respect to Holtan Hills, the plat application for phase 1 of the
      project has been submitted and the Traffic Department has determined that the
       trip generation for phase 1 does not hit the minimum threshold for imposing the
       traffic study requirement. That said, this may change as platting actions for
      additional phases of the project come forward.

Again, Tiffany and Greg are cc’d for any follow up questions.

I’ve also cc’ing Bill Falsey for further follow up, as he will be stepping back into the
Municipal Manager’s shoes after my departure. It has pleasure working productively
with you all on Girdwood issues.

All the Best,

Becky

In 2025, the Anchorage Water & Wastewater Utility (AWWU) decided to explore options for a new
primary water supply source for Girdwood to ensure that any major infrastructure investment will best
meet the community’s future water needs. Based on continuing water master planning efforts and
AWWU’s understanding of anticipated development in Girdwood, it became clear that an additional
water source would be required in Girdwood in the near future.

AWWU has completed a detailed evaluation of potential sites for developing a new water source in
Girdwood. The analysis considered a complex array of factors, including site accessibility, available well
information and understanding of hydrogeologic conditions in the area, proximity to existing water and
sanitary sewer infrastructure, land use considerations (zoning and land use designations), regulatory
considerations for treatment (surface vs groundwater, emerging contaminants), hydraulic operations
and criteria, production capability of the sources, floodplain status, and Water Master Planning
considerations – redundancy, storage, etc.

Four sites were identified as having the best potential to meet the project criteria and goals for the
development of a new water source. Those four sites were:
Alternative 1 - This alternative considered the use of AWWU’s existing main water source, Well 2, and
developing additional well(s) on a parcel adjacent to the existing well site near the Girdwood Airport.
Alternative 2 – New Girdwood Townsite Tract 17B - AWWU conducted preliminary groundwater and soil
investigations for this potential well site.
Alternative 3 – Adjacent to the Holtan Hills development. It is unlikely a high-yield well could be developed
anywhere within the Holtan Hills subdivision on the west side of Glacier Creek due to the absence of thick
alluvial deposits away from the creek and the presence of shallow bedrock. In the absence of good
groundwater in this area, this alternative considered the installation of a horizontal well (via horizontal
directional drilling) beneath Glacier Creek at the southern edge of the Holtan Hills subdivision.
Alternative 4 –This alternative would involve the purchase of private property in New Girdwood Townsite,
where it might be possible to develop and operate a high-yielding well that may not need to be treated
according to surface water rules, thereby decreasing treatment costs and complexity.
AWWU leadership, engineers, and water treatment leads along with consultants with subject matter
expertise evaluated and ranked the alternatives during an Alternative Selection and Decision-Making
Workshop held on February 11, 2026. Based on the recommendations from the evaluation, the proposed
project for an additional water source in Girdwood includes:
    •  A new, high production water well (Well 3). It is anticipated that the new well would be located
        to the northeast of the existing well site.
    •  A new, backup well that would replace Well 2.
    •  A direct filtration and UV disinfection system. Backwash water from the filtration system would
      be routed to the existing sanitary sewer system.
    •  A new approximately 40-foot by 70-foot water treatment plant (WTP) building to accommodate
       the new treatment system and associated piping and appurtenances. It is anticipated that the

Girdwood Public Water System – New Water Source


      new building will be constructed adjacent to the existing building to keep the existing system
        online until the new building is ready for service. An approximate 2-acre property acquisition
      would be  required  for developing the new treatment  plant.  It  is  anticipated  that an
       Intergovernmental Agreement within the Municipality of Anchorage (MOA) for AWWU to use
        Heritage Land Bank (HLB) land to the north (Parcel #07531109000, part of Holtan Hills Tr 4) would
      be sought for the new well site and water treatment plant.
    •   For disinfection purposes, a new on-site hypochlorite generation system, new chemical feed
       systems (coagulant & hypochlorite systems), and associated piping and appurtenances.
    •  Decommissioning wells Obs. 87-1, 87-2, 87-3 (near the existing wells) per the Alaska Best
      Management Practices For Maintaining or Decommissioning Water Wells and Boreholes
        subsections 6.2.D.2.a.i and 6.2.F. Also, decommissioning the test well on Lot 17b in New
      Girdwood Townsite (NGT).

The total estimated construction cost for the selected alternative (Alternative 1) in 2026 dollars is
approximately $20,500,000, with an estimated annual operation and maintenance (O&M) cost of
approximately $1,730,000.
AWWU is moving into the design of Alternative 1, and anticipates the following schedule for the design
and construction of a new water source in Girdwood:

WHITTIER POLICE DEPARTMENT
              Special Activity Report - Fourth of July Weekend

                                   Reporting Period: July 3-5, 2026
Executive Summary
During the July 4th weekend reporting period, WPD documented 79 total calls for service from July 3 through July 5,
2026. Activity was concentrated in Girdwood with 59 calls (75%), followed by Whittier with 17 calls (22%) and Other
areas with 3 calls (4%). Security checks accounted for 29 calls and are included in the total call count; excluding
security checks, officers handled 50 operational calls.

Key Points
•   Total calls: 79 over the three-day holiday weekend.
•   Operational calls excluding security checks: 50.
•   Traffic-related activity was the largest operational category with 17 calls, including traffic stops, traffic
    enforcement, REDDI/reckless driving, traffic complaints, and traffic hazards.
•   Proactive activity remained high with 29 security checks and 5 foot patrols.
•   Notable calls included 2 hit-and-run reports, 3 medical calls, 1 fireworks complaint, 1 welfare check, 1
    trespassing call, 1 missing person call, and 1 physical fight.
•  No death-related call type was identified in the provided data.

Narrative Summary
The July 4th weekend produced a mix of holiday-related public safety activity, proactive patrols, traffic enforcement,
and routine calls for service. Girdwood accounted for the majority of documented activity, with a substantial number
of security checks, foot patrols, traffic calls, parking problems, noise complaints, and two hit-and-run related calls.
Whittier activity included public assists, medical calls, traffic enforcement, a fireworks complaint, a welfare check,
trespassing, a missing person call, and other service-related responses.

Traffic-related calls were the leading operational category. The dataset included traffic stops, traffic enforcement,
reckless driving complaints, a REDDI report, a traffic hazard, and a traffic complaint. This indicates a significant
enforcement and roadway-safety component during the holiday weekend.

Security checks were a major portion of the call volume and appear to reflect proactive area checks during the
holiday period. These checks were especially concentrated in Girdwood, including Alyeska, Arlberg, Hightower,
Mount Hood, Toadstool, Lindblad, Egloff, and Seward Highway-area locations. Whittier security check activity was
also documented.

                            Roads and Drainages
Road Status: It has been a busy spring/early summer for road maintenance and projects. The
following items have been completed:
   •  Spring sweeping of all paved roads collected 400 tons of debris from the roads
   •  Spring grading and compaction of all gravel roads has been completed. 50,000 lbs of
       calcium chloride have been applied to the gravel roads for dust suppression and road
       hardening. We have another 20,000 lbs in reserve to reapply to main connectors as
       needed.
   •  Drainage work completed on Vail, St. Johann, Alpine Meadows, Northland, Alta,
       Brighton, Alyeska View, Lake Tahoe, Mount Hood, Arlberg, Olympic Mountain Loop,
       Jewel Mine, Timberline and Crystal Mountain. The work consisted of reshaping the
        ditch, lowering driveway culverts, adding more road material to improve drainage, and
       replacing culverts. We also addressed areas that had chronic icing issues this winter.
   •  All paved road traffic-painted lines have been repainted. All traffic signs have been
       repaired and will be addressed as problems arise.
   •  After the Blueberry Festival, crack seal all asphalt and do asphalt patch repairs
   •  Plan for ditching and road surface work in Old Town on Gold Avenue and Old West in
        late August
   •  Another round of projects and maintenance of roads will happen in the late summer/early
         fall after we complete the rebid of the roads contract in August. In the meantime, GVSA
        staff will be making brushing improvements in various spots throughout the service area
        to open the line of sight and improve drainage access as needed.
   •  Currently have ITB for 1200 tons of e-chips with 6% salt for winter traction control

being advertised by MOA Purchasing to solicit bids from professional firms to provide the
design services for the construction of the new culvert. The selection committee is currently
considering the proposals.  Still on pace to be constructed in summer 2027.

Winner Creek Trail Bridge at the Glacier Creek crossing: A contract has been signed with
Spernak and Sons for them to procure the bridge construction materials and build the bridge. We
have a pre-construction meeting with the contractor this week to kick off the project and confirm
the construction schedule. This project will start this summer and be completed next summer in
2027. The materials needed for this project have long lead times, and recent disruptions in
global markets have led to unforeseen increases in material, freight, and fuel costs. Besides the
challenges this project already faces because of its location, these unforeseen market conditions
only add more work to complete this great bridge for the community.

GVSA Road Maintenance contract: The five-year contract with Western ended in April, but we
extended it by 120 days to work with Purchasing to establish a new bid that meets their updated
requirements. In April, we had a meeting with Purchasing to determine how we should correctly
account for summer construction work and pay Davis-Bacon wages to the contractor for the
work performed. We finally worked out documents and equipment specifications that the
Purchasing department will accept, so we can issue a contract for bidding. Eagle River roads are
in the same position, so we’re worked with them to flesh out the language that purchasing
approves. All documents for bidding the new GVSA have been submitted to Public Works
Administration leadership for their review. I am hoping they complete their review this week so
we can get it over to MOA Purchasing to solicit bids from contractors. The goal is to complete
the Invitation to Bid process so we have a new contract in place by October 1st.

Whereas, Girdwood Parks and Recreation and Girdwood Turnagain Arm Lions Club (GTLC) decided to build a
picnic pavilion in the Lions’ Club Park to increase usage of the park; and

Whereas, Girdwood Parks and Recreation, with GTLC’s support, was awarded a major grant to build the
pavilion; and

Whereas, over several years, GTLC raised the $27,000 required for the grant; and

Whereas, the pavilion has been built and is well used; and

Whereas, GTLC desires to name this municipal pavilion for long-time Lion and Girdwood resident John
Trautner; and

Whereas, John Trautner died in 2022, exceeding the Public Naming Commission minimum of 36 months; and

Whereas, The John Trautner Pavilion will memorialize John’s decades of generosity to the people of Girdwood
and dedication to Alaska and Girdwood Lions;

THEREFORE, the Girdwood Board of Supervisors strongly supports the name of the new pavilion in Lions
Club Park to be The John Trautner Pavilion.
